name: molaro
description: Stream and analyze molecular dynamics trajectories in VS Code, over SSH. GPU-rendered 3D viewer, a command grammar, and Python mods that run next to your data.

molaro.assistant.model.description: Anthropic model the analysis assistant uses.

molaro.modsDir.description: Directory where mods (*.py) are stored, loaded from, and saved to. A leading ~ expands to your home directory. Empty (the default) means the global ~/.molaro/mods, shared across all workspaces. The directory is created on first use.

molaro.assistant.useStub.description: Use the scripted stub backend instead of the real Claude Agent SDK assistant (no network, no API key). For development and the test suite.

molaro.viewer.depthVariant.description: Impostor depth path: 1 = flat sprite depth (early-Z preserved), 2 = analytic per-fragment depth (correct interpenetration — required for real oriented geometry such as the ribbon to compose with sprites). Default 2, an architectural call made without hardware measurement; set 1 if frame rate matters more than crossing correctness on your hardware. Takes effect when a viewer panel is (re)opened.

molaro.viewer.maxFrames.markdownDescription: How many trajectory frames to LOAD from a real dataset. A longer trajectory is loaded with a stride — every `ceil(frames/cap)`-th frame — which keeps the frame count, and every per-frame channel a mod produces from it, bounded however long the run was; the header's provenance then names the stride and the true frame count. `0` (the default) uses the producer's built-in cap of 500 frames. A positive number caps at that many. A negative number loads **every** frame — correct for short trajectories, but a 15 000-frame system then makes a per-point per-frame vector channel of `frames x atoms x 3 x 4` bytes (2.33 GB on a 12 944-atom system), which will not fit. Takes effect when a viewer panel is (re)opened.

enumDescriptions: Infer every missing bond, solvent included.
Infer missing bonds, but skip solvent residues.
Draw only the bonds the topology declares.
molaro.viewer.inferBonds.markdownDescription: Whether to INFER the covalent bonds a topology does not declare. Many real files leave connectivity out: a PDB with no `CONECT` records shows every ligand and lipid as loose dust (the 222 227-atom membrane system: 482 DMPC lipids, 56 876 atoms, fully unbonded), and mdtraj's residue templates never bond nucleic `O3'-P`, so **every** nucleic backbone arrives unlinked. `full` (the default) fills those in from Cordero covalent radii, scoped to within one residue, to the named backbone linkage between sequence-adjacent residues (protein `C-N`, nucleic `O3'-P`), and to S/Se crosslinks (disulfide, thioether) — additively, so no bond the file declares is ever removed and no coordinate is touched. `nonsolvent` does the same but skips solvent residues: on the membrane that is 67 058 fewer inferred bonds and about half the inference cost, at the price of unbonded water. `off` draws only declared bonds, reproducing the pre-inference edge list exactly. `Header.provenance` names the per-scope counts whenever inference added anything, the status line appends the inferred count to the edge count, and its hover carries the producer's full sentence — including what inference does NOT reach (metal-organic bonds, glycosidic and isopeptide links, head-to-tail cyclic peptides). Cost, MEASURED on the 222 227-atom membrane, cold open: `off` 4.79 s / 50 488 edges / 5.17 MB header; `nonsolvent` 5.16 s / 106 882 edges / 6.07 MB; `full` 5.45 s / 173 940 edges / 7.28 MB — inference itself is 0.60 s of that. The 41% larger header also costs the webview: `JSON.parse` of it goes 20 ms → 36 ms (the added payload is 123 452 two-element arrays, which cost far more per byte than the scalar arrays that dominate the rest), and retained memory about +45 MB. Click-picking scans every edge, so it goes 2.6 ms → 7.7 ms per pick on that system; `nonsolvent` or `off` is the lever if a paint gesture feels heavy there. Takes effect when a viewer panel is (re)opened.

molaro.pythonPath.markdownDescription:
Python interpreter for the data producer. Needs `numpy`, and `mdtraj >= 1.11` for real trajectories (**1.10 is not supported** — its `Residue.is_nucleic` raises instead of answering). `~` is expanded. Empty falls back to the `VIEWER_PYTHON` environment variable, then `python3`.

**On a remote host, use this setting, not the environment.** VS Code's CLI keeps a long-lived daemon that spawns every server as its child, so extension hosts inherit the daemon's environment rather than your shell's — an export in `.bashrc` may never be seen.

molaro.modTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription:
Wall-clock budget for a single mod run, in seconds. The producer's own floor is 5 s; `0` falls back to it rather than disabling the guard, because this is a hang guard and should be raisable but not removable.

Raise it on a shared or busy machine: a mod's cost is wall clock, so someone else's I/O storm can push a 2 s computation past a 5 s cap. Lowering `#molaro.viewer.maxFrames#` cuts the cost itself.
